claim_boundary: A five-method QC32 slicing comparison. ArcTN fixed-tree post-search slicing and ArcTN dynamic slicing consume the exact same saved Heavy SSA path for each circuit and repeat. Cotengra post-search slicing, Cotengra Dynamic slicing and OMECO TreeSA8 plus TreeSASlicer8 are independent native-library baselines.

objective.native_selection_boundary: ArcTN Heavy path search and dynamic completed-round ranking use pure FLOPs. ArcTN fixed-tree leg choice is the library's deterministic target-feasibility heuristic and has no objective argument. Cotengra receives minimize='flops'. OMECO TreeSA is pure FLOPs, while TreeSASlicer uses its native FLOPs-directed target-space penalty. Common exact total sliced FLOPs is the reported comparison metric, not a claim that every native slicer ranks candidates by the identical formula.

target.meaning: largest single intermediate tensor in one slice, measured in elements
target.not_equivalent_to: process RSS or a complete execution memory limit

queue.description: The fixed-tree ArcTN row is queued first and atomically saves one Heavy path for every circuit and repeat. The following ArcTN dynamic row must load that exact path. Whenever one eight-core slot is released, the next pending cell starts immediately.

shared_heavy_path.path_equality_rule: The consumer must load the producer artifact and the harness must report the same input SSA path. Dynamic slicing may change only its delivered output path.

methods.mechanism: Run the frozen Heavy path search once, then choose sliced indices on that fixed contraction tree without changing the SSA path.
Load the exact Heavy SSA path saved by the paired fixed-tree row; alternate slicing with subtree reconfiguration and rank completed rounds by total sliced FLOPs.
Complete the unsliced AutoHQ path search first, then slice the returned contraction tree. The slicing stage does not run inside the hyper-optimization trials.
Dynamic slicing during hyper-optimization; slice selection alternates with local contraction-tree reconfiguration.

methods.entrypoint: omeco.optimize_code(..., TreeSA(...)) followed by omeco.slice_code(..., TreeSASlicer(...))
methods.repeat_semantics: deterministic repeated execution for runtime variability only; quality is counted once per circuit because OMECO 0.2.6 uses fixed internal trial seeds

timing_boundary.planner_api_wall_seconds: The native path-search and slicing API stages, recorded separately when the method has multiple stages.
timing_boundary.arctn_shared_path_accounting: The Heavy path is physically searched once per circuit and repeat. For a logical end-to-end comparison, add the same saved Heavy path-search wall to each ArcTN slicing-stage wall; report the shared setup and slicing stage separately as well.
timing_boundary.exact_replay_wall_seconds_before_write: Common exact validation and path conversion after the native API returns, measured before JSON serialization and persistence.
timing_boundary.external_wall_seconds: Worker process launch through complete process exit; this is the one-hour hard-limit boundary.
timing_boundary.classification: Shared-server, concurrent throughput observations; not isolated single-cell latency.

phase_boundary.this_package: path search and slicing quality only
phase_boundary.fixed_plan_execution: separate optional campaign after successful plans are sealed
phase_boundary.e2e_rule: If execution is run later, report planning and execution separately before any summed end-to-end value.

analysis_population.all_terminal_population: All 800 cells, with every failure retained.
analysis_population.strict_cross_library_population: The 20 scalar-output circuits, where all methods have no output indices available to slice.
analysis_population.internal_slicing_full_corpus_population: All 32 circuits for ArcTN and Cotengra, restricted to internal-index slicing.
analysis_population.omeco_non_scalar_output_boundary: OMECO TreeSASlicer has no public allow_outer=False or excluded-index control. Its 12 non-scalar-output cases are supplementary and must report any sliced output indices explicitly.
analysis_population.repeat_aggregation: Aggregate five repeats within each seeded or repeated method and circuit first. OMECO quality is counted once per circuit because its five executions are deterministic repeats; use those five only for runtime variability. Then compute paired geometric means across circuits, and also report all-terminal coverage and common-success results.
